$comment: Seconds each browser test file runs in one of CI's docs browser jobs (4 cores, the files several at a time, so the time a file takes beside others): what packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js splits the files into TEST_SHARD's shares by (`--shard-weights`, apps/docs/package.json's test:browser), longest first, each to the share with the least so far. A file not named here weighs the median of these, and the log of its job says so. A name of a file that is not here is ignored. Measured again from CI runs 42411078574 and 42415970600 (2026-11-07, each job's `# file-duration` lines), the mean of the two. Keep them current: a file they do not weigh, or weigh at half its time, lands in a job it overfills. To measure them again: every job sharded by these weights prints `# file-duration <file> <seconds>` (the duration of the file's own run) at the end of its log; save the logs of a run's jobs (`gh run view <run> --job <job> --log > shard-N.log`) and run `node packages/tools/src/shard-weights.js apps/docs/test/browser/durations.json shard-1.log shard-2.log shard-3.log`. `$alone` lists the files that take a CI job of their own (packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js, balance): the fixture gallery keeps the job's cores busy for its whole run, and beside it the Button page took more than 30 s to load in WebKit (run 40329390452), so it runs alone and the others share the remaining jobs.
